body.statement: Uniformly over every deterministic binary schedule \(Y\) satisfying the stated design and stratified-interference conditions, \[\Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\in\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}\ge 1-\alpha.\] The covered object is the complete weak order, so the assertion simultaneously covers all policy ranks, every partial tie pattern, and every zero-variance face. No pairwise allocation of \(\alpha\) and no cross-arm covariance estimator enters the construction. As an immediate reporting corollary, for each \(r\in\mathcal R\), take the union of the integer positions occupied by \(r\) over the retained weak orders, letting a tied block contribute every position that it spans. With the same probability, these rank sets simultaneously contain every policy's true tied-rank interval.
body.justification: This is the missing finite-sample simultaneous coverage theorem for exact-quota policy rankings.
body.gap: Mogstad et al. require a valid simultaneous difference region, Rigdon and Hudgens cover scalar effects, and Liu, Shaikh, and Zhong reserve finite-sample validity for stronger individual-level restrictions rather than the weak average welfare order.
body.consumer: RCT2 and the Baird--Bohren--McIntosh--\u00d6zler design calculator can report which complete and tied policy orderings remain compatible with the realized experiment at level \(1-\alpha\).
body.proof_tex:
First, the order being covered is causal rather than an observed-law ranking.  For a cluster of response type \(t\), uniform assignment of exactly \(k_r\) treated units makes the treatment probability of every unit equal to \(k_r/n\).  Therefore its randomization-average cluster mean under quota policy \(r\) is
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}
 \left\{\left(1-\frac{k_r}{n}\right)Y_{ci}(0,r)
 +\frac{k_r}{n}Y_{ci}(1,r)\right\}
 =\frac{(n-k_r)(N_r^{10}+N_r^{11})
 +k_r(N_r^{01}+N_r^{11})}{n^2}
 =u_{tr}.
\]
Here the first equality uses exact second-stage randomization and fixed potential outcomes, and the second uses the response-type counts.  Averaging this fixed quota-policy welfare over the \(C\) clusters gives \(U_r(N^\star)=C^{-1}\sum_tN_t^\star u_{tr}\).  Thus \(\mathcal O(N^\star)\) is the complete weak order of the fixed finite-population causal welfares; \(\widehat U(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) is used only to form the randomization discrepancy.

By true-count compatibility, \(N^\star\in\mathcal N(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\) for every assignment realization.  On the event \(p_{N^\star}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})>\alpha\), the definition of the order confidence set therefore puts \(\mathcal O(N^\star)\) in \(\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\).  Consequently
\[
 \left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}
 \subseteq
 \left\{p_{N^\star}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\le\alpha\right\}.
\]
Applying schedule-level super-uniformity with \(N=N^\star\) and \(q=\alpha\) gives
\[
 \Pr_{A\sim\pi_{\exp}}\left\{\mathcal O(N^\star)\notin
 \widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})\right\}
 \le\alpha,
\]
which is the asserted coverage.  Every step is pointwise in the fixed binary schedule, so the bound is uniform over the stated schedule class.  Discreteness, ties, and zero-variance faces require no separate argument because super-uniformity was proved with the weak right tail.

For the reporting corollary, write any retained weak order as descending tied blocks \((B_1,\ldots,B_J)\).  If \(r\in B_j\), its occupied-position set is
\[
 \rho_{\mathcal O}(r)=
 \left\{1+\sum_{\ell<j}|B_\ell|,\ldots,
 \sum_{\ell\le j}|B_\ell|\right\}.
\]
On the coverage event the true weak order is retained, and hence, simultaneously for every \(r\),
\[
 \rho_{\mathcal O(N^\star)}(r)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{\mathcal O\in\widehat{\mathfrak O}_{\alpha}(H^{\mathrm{obs}})}
 \rho_{\mathcal O}(r).
\]
This is exactly simultaneous containment of all true tied-rank intervals.
